utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Good morning. Today Judge Parker is not able to sit, so in application of Rule 15 bis, Judge Thelin and I will sit in this session. We hope Judge Parker will be able to sit tomorrow, but today it will be Judge Thelin and myself. Good morning, sir. May I please ask you to read the affirmation that is on the card held in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the record the Prosecution is called witness Fatmir Kamberi

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Kamberi, do you recall providing an information to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2004?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall meeting with a lady from the registry who certified your statement in 2005?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall providing additional information that same day which was also certified?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters wish to note that the witness is answering in Macedonian so perhaps he is listening to interpretation in the Macedonian language. If that could be checked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir. It appears that you are listening to the interpretation --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Can the usher perhaps take care of that?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you receiving the translation in Albanian, Mr. Kamberi, now?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Kamberi, before coming here have you had the opportunity to read both documents?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that its content is correct and accurate?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution will seek to tender the statement of 2004 and the addendum of 2005 according to Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P426, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The witness, Fatmir Kamberi, is a Ljuboten resident of Albanian ethnicity. On the 10th of August, 2001, the Macedonian forces began shelling and shooting Ljuboten from positions in the mountains. On the 11th, there was occasional gun-fire. At around 2.00 a.m., on the morning of the 12th, the witness observed three to four uniformed persons in the yard of the church carrying weapons and moving between the church and the Macedonian houses in Ljuboten. At around 4.00 a.m., the witness went to Rami Jusufi's house to have coffee. He left approximately one hour later. Around 8.00 a.m. on the 12th of August, the witness observed intensive shooting coming from the church and elsewhere. He was informed that the army and the police were entering their houses. In the afternoon women, children and the elderly began fleeing the village. The witness remained in Ljuboten. On the 13th of August, the witness saw a number of houses burn down and evidence of hand-grenades, automatic fire and a container of gas in the vicinity. On the 14th of August, the witness observed the house of an ethnic Macedonian burning. On the 15th of August, his own house was burned. In the witness addendum given in November 2005, Mr. Kamberi stated that a colleague of his who was also a relative of Mr. Tarculovski told him about the speech made by Mr. Tarculovski during the funeral on the 12th -- on the 11th of August at Ljubanci of the policemen killed in the mine incident the previous day. Johan Tarculovski said that there was an order from Boris Trajkovski and that he would take care of the people of Ljuboten the following day. Now, if we could please call 65 ter 184, page 3, ERN N000-7879.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Kamberi, in paragraph 20 of your statement, you mention that on Monday, the 13th of August, you saw houses from your neighbourhood burn and you indicated them in a document with letter C. We have now the document in front of us. Is the handwriting of the names and also the signature and the date below your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please read out loud for the record the names of the properties that you wrote down starting from the upper part left to right and then going to the bottom part, please?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please do it.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Agim Jusufi, Jusufi Rashit, Xhabir Rashiti, Qenan Jusufi, Xhevdet Jusufi, Nazmi Jusufi, Sabit Jusufi, Rami Jusufi, Halim Duraku.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender this document, this photo into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P427, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You mention in your statement that you saw these houses burn on the 13th. What did you see in the same neighbourhood on the 12th of August, the day before?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: On the 12th of August, the houses were burned. It was on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And what did you see, if anything, in that area, coming from that area?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: On the 12th of August, from afar, I saw the smoke coming. I didn't know which houses were being burned.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. In paragraph 21 of your statement and paragraph 22, you mention two more houses which were burned on the 14th of August; the house of Aleksandar Doskovski and your own house on the 15th of August. Aside from these two houses, do you know any other house which was set on fire which was burned after the weekend 10 to 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: No. Only these two houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now if we could please call 65 ter 199.22, ERN N004-4729. It's the photo A depicted in page 9 of the Court binder. And before we're waiting for the photo, Mr. Kamberi, you mention in paragraph 10 of your statement that at 2.00 a.m. in the early morning of Sunday, 12th of August, you saw uniformed people around the yard of the church but you were not sure what kind of uniforms they were. Were you able to see which colour those uniforms were?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I was about 25 metres away. It was 2.00 a.m. It was night, of course. It was dark. But because I was close enough, I could see that it was the green colour of the army, of the Macedonian army. I can't give you the hue but it was green. Whether it was lighter or darker, I don't know. But it was a military colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. Kamberi. That's enough. Now, if you could look, please, at the photo. Are you able to see here the church and if we could have, please, the usher's assistance?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the gentleman, if could you please take the pen and draw a cross where you see the church that you saw those uniformed men at 2.00 on Sunday and write number 1.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: The church? Or the yard of the church, which one?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: First a cross in the church and write number one next to the cross, please.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, if you could please, draw a circle around the yard around the area where you saw those uniformed men walking around?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: For the record the witness has drawn a circle on the upper left side of the photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And now, Mr. Kamberi, do you see the house of Rami Jusufi in this photo?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please also draw a cross and write number 2 where this house is located.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will seek to tender this photo into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P428, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, no further questions. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. You will be asked now a few questions by the Defence. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Kamberi.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kamberi, my name is Edina Residovic and together with my colleague Guenael Mettraux I appear on behalf of Mr. Ljube Boskoski. I will ask you, Mr. Kamberi, to wait for my question to be interpreted and answer only then, although you maybe understand my language as well, so Their Honours and the colleagues in the courtroom are able to hear your answer and my question, and in this way, we will best assist the Court to follow your testimony. Did you understand this, Mr. Kamberi?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were born in Ljuboten and you live there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, you lived with your wife and three children. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You graduated from the secondary school in Skopje and you worked as a salesman for seven years in a textile shop. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you opened your own shop and your shop was at Bit Pazar, not far from the butcher, Nebush. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this private shop, you worked until 2001.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: This is not the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me for how long did you work in your private shop?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: In 1999, I closed my company. In 2001, this is not the truth. It was 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your clarification. Is it correct that from 2003 until 2006 you worked in a post office?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you leave that employment in the post office?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I was there only under contract. I had a contract.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is it correct that there was a suspicion that you embezzled some money, was that the reason or was the reason that your contract had expired? What is the actual reason?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: There is a law and there is a police force and what you mentioned does not have anything to do with this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I wish that you answer before this Court under oath in regards to some information that I had as background information, and I thank you for your clarification. This is why I'm asking my questions, to have them clarified. Could you tell me, what is your occupation presently?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: At the moment I'm unemployed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So can one say that you're a farmer in your village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: A little bit of farming. Now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This year you worked quite a bit in relation to the erecting of the monument for these soldiers killed in Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: You are wrong when you say "soldiers." Those are the victims of the war, of the Ljuboten massacre.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I see now that my question is interpreted as soldiers in Ljuboten, while I actually stated you worked on the erection of the monument for the people killed in Ljuboten. I never mentioned the word "soldiers." Is it correct, Mr. Kamberi, that -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: You mentioned the word "soldiers," and I said that they were victims of the Ljuboten massacre, and the child Erxan Aliu, could not be a soldier. Of course, it is true that I worked five months voluntarily --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Kamberi, that was a mistake made in the interpretation of my question. I never mentioned the word "soldiers" and you only received the interpretation "soldiers" and I please ask you, let us continue asking the questions. I understood what you stated. Is it correct, Mr. Kamberi, that you were aware that in 2001 there was a crisis situation in Macedonia because of the attacks of the NLA groups against the Macedonian forces of the army of the police and the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You could follow those news on a daily basis on the TV. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The crisis was particularly intensive in the areas of Tetovo and Kumanovo but also in the vicinity of Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your village, Ljuboten, belongs to the Cair municipality. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: It used to be. Now it is in Butel. In 2001, it was in Cair.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Cair and Butel are component parts of the city of Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes. They are communes on their own, municipalities on their own.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ljuboten has a location that is of exceptional importance for the defence of the city of Skopje. Are you aware of this, is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will try and ask you a question that you will be able to understand. Is it correct that Ljuboten is located on the slopes of Skopska Crna Gora mountain?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Skopska Crna Gora is a connection between the Republic of Macedonia and the southern Serbia and Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Listen, in Skopska Crna Gora, if you count the villages, Brnjarci, Treshov [phoen], Stijkovc, Bulacan, Rastak, Ljubanci, Pobozje, Kucavista, Gluvo, Mirkovci, Banjani, Cucer, Sandevo, Radasani, all these are villages where Macedonians live, ethnic Macedonians, and some villages that are Serb villages, the only Albanian village is Ljuboten, in the midst of all of them. Ljuboten -- you're saying that Ljuboten is on the border with Kosovo, but Ljubanci and the other Macedonian villages, Gluva and so on, are closer to that border. From Ljuboten to the Kosova border, there are other villages in between, behind Ljuboten. There are 37 kilometres or 40 kilometres from Ljuboten to the border.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your detailed answer but my question was a bit different. I did not ask whether Ljuboten is at the border with Kosovo or with southern Serbia. I asked that Skopska Crna Gora is the mountain bordering with southern Serbia and Kosovo. So please answer, are you aware of this or not?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And all locations that you mentioned, Ljuboten among them, are located on the slopes of Skopska Crna Gora mountain and are close to the border with the southern Serbia and Kosovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I already told you that the distance is 40 kilometres, and there are other villages, Strima, Malino, Brest, Tanusevci, Gosince, behind they are close to the border, towards the border, while Ljuboten is sort of a settlement of Skopje. If you say that Ljuboten borders that border, then you can as well say that Skopje borders that border.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kamberi, I would like to ask you to listen carefully to my question and answer that question.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I am hearing you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We are grateful for your questions, but I never said that Ljuboten was at the border. Allow me to ask you the following. Is it correct that because of the position of Skopska Crna Gora mountain and the villages that are there, Skopska Crna Gora is of particular importance for the defence of the city of Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: For the defence of the city of Skopje, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: At what risk could Skopje possibly be from Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please answer my question, whether Skopska Crna Gora is of interest for the defence of the city of Skopje. If you don't know, just state that you don't know.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: From whom should Skopje be defended? From Ljuboten? What strategy are you talking about here? I enumerated 20 villages of Macedonians, then Skopje should be under risk from those villages. They would pose danger, those 25 villages that I have enumerated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As opposed to you, the army of the Republic of Macedonia considered it to be a region of particular importance for the defence of the city of Skopje, and in June it passed a decision to deploy military forces in the area of Skopska Crna Gora. Was that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that since June part of the army forces were positioned above the village of Ljuboten as well?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that the transcript didn't pick up correctly the previous answer. The witness said "I know."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Skopska Crna Gora was the natural connection from the Macedonian side between the Kumanovo region and Kosovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you could start from Kumanovo and via Skopska Crna Gora mountain come to the border with Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: You mean from Kumanovo?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: It could be.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that you can see very well the valley of the city of Skopje from the village of Ljuboten from various locations but especially from the new mosque?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell that you Ljuboten is mainly agricultural village where the population was involved in farming, in agriculture, you would certainly agree with me?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I would agree with you, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you can agree with me if I state that part of the population of Ljuboten, even before 2001, were involved in various activities against the state of Macedonia. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that some hostile activities of individuals started very soon after the declaration of independence of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you maybe it would refresh your memory that in 1992, a decision about the system of national defence was passed, a Book of Rules on the system of national defence, headquarters of the Armed Forces of the Albanians and battalion for the protection of the Cair municipality that gathering of data on about 1.300 military conscripts which composed the Albanian forces started. And that on the 6th of June 2003, the paramilitary unit for the village of Ljuboten was requested to be established and it started, and also formation list for the military unit for the village of Ljuboten had started with certain command of units and the necessary weapons for the units, then, this would refresh your memory, that this took place in the course of 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the year before was 1993 and not 2003.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: There is the first time I hear about this from you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you heard that in June 1994, the municipal court Skopje II in Skopje sentenced Mithad Emini, Hasan Agushi and eight more individuals for offences organising to perform hostile activities and among the charges was also the establishment of paramilitary independent unit for the village of Ljuboten, gathering staff for that unit and those individuals then bought 200 automatic rifles of Chinese origin. Did you know that in 1994 ten persons were sentenced for participating in these activities?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: To my knowledge, nobody from Ljuboten was sentenced. Only someone else, or you, in person, know about these things. Personally, I have no knowledge whatsoever. This is the first time I hear about it. Actually, you're the first person to tell me that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The aforementioned sentenced persons are not from Ljuboten but the unit they established was supposed to be stationed at Ljuboten. You're not aware of that either. Is it so?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: These are lies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Kamberi, that immediately at the beginning of the crisis in 2001, some individuals from Ljuboten joined the NLA?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I don't know about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that individuals from Ljuboten participated in the fights at Aracinovo and Tanusevci villages?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the youngsters controlled the entrance into the village of Ljuboten as early as in the spring of 2001?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: This is not correct. Because in Ljuboten village the police regularly caught patrol whenever they wanted, and the entrance to the village of Ljuboten was controlled by the Macedonian forces with the check-points that they had established, not the way you're putting it to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, in Ljuboten itself where Albanian population lives, there was never a police check-point. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I'm not saying in Ljuboten itself, but the patrols could patrol the village whenever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you agree with me if I say that as early in the spring of 2001, Ljuboten becomes an important logistics location for the needs of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: This is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that because of the larger scale conflicts in the region of Kumanovo where there were very strict controls by the army and the police, Ljuboten was practically used for supply of food and other provisions to the NLA groups that were fighting around Kumanovo?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: This is not true, because as I already told you the village of Ljuboten was not only surrounded by policemen and army, but it was surrounded or amidst 25 other Macedonian villages, on all sides, north, south, east, west. It was surrounded by Macedonian villages, and nobody could dare supply with food or other provisions. Not a single bird could fly freely without them knowing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you agree, Mr. Kamberi, if I say that in March 2001, NLA members came to Ljuboten to make propaganda among the local population, to make the population join the NLA?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: This is not true. Excuse me, the Macedonian army were at Ljuboten. A person from Rastak, I don't know who he was, at the local community, he was there together with a co-villager from Rastak and they were Macedonians. The KLA - correction - NLA were not there. These are not -- these things that you are saying are not true. The Macedonian army had access to that area whenever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you agree with me, Mr. Kamberi, that after March of 2001, a large number of villagers actively joined the NLA while another part of the villagers supported the NLA activities in different ways? Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? I did not understand it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking whether it is correct and could you agree with me if I say that as early in the spring of 2001, a large number of villagers of Ljuboten joined the NLA units while --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: What is that, NLA units?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These are the NLA units, active in the area of Skopska Crna Gora mountain.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: These things are not true. And the NLA was never active in the mountain of Skopska Crna Gora.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can I ask that the witness is shown now 65 ter 1D539, 1D4897.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document was received from the Prosecutor under the Rule 68, and this is part of a diary written in the Albanian language, and I would like to ask that the page 1D489 [as interpreted] be shown in the Albanian, and the page 1D4901 in the English language. And I would like to ask that the second page of the diary is shown in the Albanian version, so that one can see the second page. It is not important for the first page to be displayed. On the first page, on the left-hand side page you only see the dates 26th and 27th of March, while in the last paragraph of this diary it is stated, so -- the dates are 26th and 27th of March, 2001. And it is stated: "At 1720 [Previous translation continues]... [In English] In the direction of Gosince towards the region of the fields parts of the special unit were taken away at 1630 hours by orders from Ljuboten with attention by UCK." [Interpretation] Mr. Kamberi, do you know that in Ljuboten at that moment the liaison officer between Ljuboten and NLA was Commander Lisi.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, due to the importance of this document in relation to the Ljuboten events, I would seek to tender this document as exhibit. As I said, we received this document from the Prosecution on the basis of Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this WITNESS has not acknowledged and has no basis to acknowledge what the information which is contained in this document. So I don't see how document could be admitted through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: We don't receive it, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Kenan Salievski?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Kenan Salievski, in 2001, was the chairman of the Crisis Staff in Ljuboten village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If Kenan Salievski, in his statement to the Office of the Prosecutor dated 6 November and 7th November 2004, in paragraph 40 said the following: "[In English] Being asked who from Ljuboten villagers were members of NLA, I say that Suat Saliu, Riza Jonuzi, Besim Murtezani, Rafiz Bajrami, Shefajet Bajrami, Fikret Aliu, Nimet Aliu, Ruhan Jashari or Bajrami, Ramadan Alimi killed in Matejce mountains, Musa Selimi, Refedin Selimi, Faik Murati, Shefket Murati, Zecir Murati, and Rasim Murati, I think there were about 18 people, but I don't know -- remember all names." [Interpretation] Would this statement, Mr. Kenan Salievski's statement be in contradiction with what you just said before this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Listen, who has been part of what I cannot give you evidence here about these things. I'm not a policeman. I had my own business to tend to. I minded my own things, and everybody who might have been in the NLA, these was a secret of theirs. These were secret things that they didn't tell anybody else about. I didn't know about them. I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said previously that nobody from the village was member of the NLA. All I'm doing is asking now if the statement of Mr. Kenan Salievski is contrary to what you said before this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I'm not a registry officer, and I don't keep records of who goes where, so I think I'm clear: I don't have information about what you're asking.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kamberi, feel free to speak in your native language and it will be interpreted to me. Thank you. Do you know Suat Saliu?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I do know him. Is he a co-villager of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you probably know that he was a member of the NLA too.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: No, I had no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if Suat Saliu, in his statement to the Prosecutor dated 25th October 2003, enumerated a number of Ljuboten inhabitants who were members of the NLA, his statement would again be in contradiction with what you said, that there were no NLA members from the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I don't know about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Zemri Zendeli?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I know almost everybody in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He is the Muslim priest, the hoxha of the village, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If, in his statement to the OTP he said the following: "[In English] If I knew Riza Jonuzi, Rasim Murati, Arsim Elezi, Faredin Murati, Faik Murati, Shefajet Bajrami, Besim Murtezani, Jetulla Rifi, Bekri Ajdini, Orhan Bajrami, Shefket Murati, Refedin Selimi, Feriz Selimi, Suat Saliu, Rafiz Bajrami, I say yes, I know all of except Faredin Murati. All of them are from Ljuboten. Being asked whether I knew if they were members NLA in the period between 10 and 12 August, I say yes, they were." [Interpretation] Mr. Kamberi, would this statement of a neighbour of yours, the village Imam, be, again, contradictory to what you said before this Trial Chamber, that there were no NLA members in the village?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I already told you, I'm not a civil servant to keep evidence of who of my co-villagers has gone where and what they are. I live in the Macedonian part of the village. On the other side of the village, we go very rarely to do some farming, jobs, and we pass in transit there by tractor. And I don't keep lists of people where they are and who they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Baki Halimi, Mr. Kamberi?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You previously said that you were not aware of the fact that he was a Commander Lisi?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I only know him as Baki Halimi.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In my previous question on whether you were engaged in the erection of the monument at Ljuboten, you did not give me any answer. Were you involved in these activities for erecting this monument?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I already gave you an answer. I worked there for four -- for five months in a row.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in August, this monument was unveiled. Correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to the inhabitants, there were many people present, who were invited and the villagers, the local population was addressed by Ali Ahmeti. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Halimi Baki, Commander Lisi also addressed the crowd. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: You are calling him Commander Lisi. To me he is Baki Halimi.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to tell you that Baki Halimi was the main link between the NLA and the individuals from the village and that in this capacity he spread propaganda, mobilised the villagers to join the NLA, this would be correct. Right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that Kenan Salievski in the statement that I mentioned earlier which he gave to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 6th and 7th of November 2004, in this statement he said the following: "[In English] Contacts with NLA, was Baki Halimi, alias Commander Lisi, from our village. Alimi was for a long time handed his activity, but I found out that he had contact with NLA. Saliu Naim [phoen], Rexhepi Supi [phoen], both from Ljuboten, told me about Alimi's contacts with NLA because they were close to him." [Interpretation] You would agree with me that this statement, given by Kenan Salievski, is totally contrary to what you said, that Baki Halimi was not Commander Lisi and had nothing to do with the NLA, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Baki Halimi, I know him as a teacher in the school, and I don't know anything further about him. In regard to Qenan Salievski's statements, I'm doubtful about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, or, rather, did you hear the name of Nazim Bushi?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I have heard it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You heard that he was a commander of the 114th Brigade of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If in his statement dated 9 and 10th June 2004, Bushi Nazim --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: This is the fourth time that my learned colleague is using a statement and we didn't receive notice that this four statements will be used. We have received just now before cross a list, but these statements are not included here. So this is already the fourth time that my learned colleagues are using documents without being giving notice.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, pursuant to the decision of the Trial Chamber, we informed the Prosecutor that we would use certain documents only for discreditation purposes. Before the cross-examination we submitted to the Prosecutor a list of documents that we might use with this witness. And this was, again, pursuant to the decision of the Trial Chamber. It is possible that only Kenan Salievski's statement was not in this list because we used it previously.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Actually, Suad Saliu, Zemri Zendeli and Nazim Bushi statements are not either in the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not use the statement of Suat Saliu, I only mentioned this person and I didn't put to this witness any part of his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I think you did, Ms. Residovic. I think you did put a number of elements of the statement of Suat Saliu to the witness. I have it in my notes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I only said that this witness spoke in his statement that there were NLA members, but I didn't quote his statement the way I quoted the statement of other persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kamberi, if Nazim Bushi has stated in his statement that I have mentioned the following. In the item 46: "[In English] On events on 10 to 12 of August 2001, I have prepared a complete overview of information about -- that I receive from Baki Halimi in that period." [Interpretation] And further on in item 52: "[In English] I received all the information Baki Halimi by the mobile phone in the period from 10 to 12 of August 2001. That is all I knew about Ljuboten events." [Interpretation] Then this link between Halimi Baki and the NLA would also be contradicting what you testified about before this Court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you, you answered my question --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: If you could repeat the question, because I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You stated previously that Halimi Baki was not the link with the NLA when I showed you the testimony of Kenan Salievski or Saliu --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, statement, not testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- you stated that this statement could be doubted. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have read to you a part of the statement of Nazim Bushi who says that between the 10th and the 12th of August, he was in touch with Baki Halimi, and I'm asking you: Is it correct that this statement of Nazim Bushi is again contradicting what you stated, that Halimi Baki had no link with the NLA?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And, otherwise, you were rather close with the Commander Lisi, Baki Halimi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I know him as a teacher, but I don't know him as Commander Lisi or Lisi.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to state to you, Mr. Kamberi, that you yourself very early at the times of the fights in the Kumanov region, were actively involve in helping or supporting the NLA, that would be correct. Is that correct.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to state to you that you were actually in charge of the logistics, that would also be correct. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to say to you that you actually then were given the name of Miskoja and you were known under that name as the person who was in charge of the logistics in the village, then this would also be correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: This is the first time I am hearing this. In the Balkans there are tigers, leopards, Tarzans, Rambos, everything. What you are saying is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, were you once leading a group of young villagers to Matejce?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: No, that's not true. I have never been to Matejce in my life.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of August, 2001, the NLA members killed eight and wounded six members of the army of the Republic of Macedonia returning from their position via a remotely activated land-mine. Is that correct? Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I heard it on the media.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the explosion of that mine, three armed persons entered the village. Do you know this?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that immediately after that a meeting was held at the school and the discussion at the meeting was how to organise the village?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I'm not aware about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I tell you that you were also at that meeting, as well as your brother Meshir and Rami Jusufi and Zemri Zendeli and others would that refresh your memory? Do you remember the meeting?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I tell that it was agreed then that check-points are organised, manned by armed persons, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's not true. What you're saying is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that after this meeting, Commander Lisi distributed ammunition. He gave 25 bullets each to you and to everyone else present there, so to Rami Jusufi as well?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: All these things are lies. Nothing is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I tell you that the first check-point was near the church, the second one near the house of Rami Jusufi, the third one behind the bridge near the Ahmeti houses while the final one was near the Muslim graveyard, would that remind you of the mode in which the village was organised?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: There was no check-point in the village, and all the things that you said are untrue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement you gave to the Prosecutor, you stated that on the 10th you moved your wife and children to the house of your brother Meshir because it was safer there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then you protected the windows to the house with -- with bags expecting that maybe there would be retaliation for the killed soldiers and someone could attack the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct. That we sheltered all the children -- all our children in the cellar of my brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you also stated, if I can re-interpret your statement, that you monitored the situation from the yard of your -- of the house, hiding behind the walls. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, otherwise, the traditional Albanian houses in Ljuboten are surrounded, fenced by walls, and it was possible for you to hide behind that wall so that you are able to observe the situation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's not correct that the villages or the houses are surrounded by walls, because the Macedonian regime, a few years ago, brought down the walls with an excavator, and the village of Aracinovo had a thousand of problems because of those walls so the situation has changed now. In my house, there are three of us, three brothers that live there and you can come and visit any time you want and you will see that there are no walls.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that this is so now, but I'm asking you whether it is correct that, in 2001 and before that the traditional Albanian house did have a wall that safeguarded the privacy of the family from anyone who would be passing down the street.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: In Ljuboten, there are no more old houses. Everybody has built a new house. Everybody is trying to get modernised and the old traditions now have been lost almost. From 2001 until today, it is the same Ljuboten. The Ljuboten of 2001 is the same with the Ljuboten today. Even the Macedonian houses are similar to our houses, and you can come and see that for yourself whenever you want.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kamberi, is it correct that on the Friday, 10th of August, in the evening many families had started already leaving the village of Ljuboten. Some went towards Skopje, while some went to the lower parts of the village where they believed it was safer?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you stated, you moved into the house of Selim Jusufi, your neighbour. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And on the following day your neighbours, so again on Saturday, August 11th, your neighbours were also leaving their houses and moving to the lower parts of the city -- of the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's true, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the wife, the mother and the children of Rami Jusufi went there, while he stayed alone at that house with his disabled father. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's not correct. Rami Jusufi's wife and children went to the lower neighbourhood. Rami Jusufi, his father, who was an invalid, and his mother, were in the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that in the night between Saturday and Sunday, you were still in the house of Selim Jusufi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you stated, around 2.00, Jetulla --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Rashiti --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- there and he informed you that he noticed movements of some people in the yard of the church. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since his house is only ten metres away from the church, you immediately went there to see it for yourself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And today when asked by my learned colleague, you clarified what you had seen there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You clarified your statement when you came to The Hague on the 4th of September, 2007, and then you stated the following to the Prosecutor: "[In English] In Paragraph 10 of my statement when I state that I could recognise three or four person in the yard of the church, they were in uniform but I couldn't see what kind of uniform they wore. I mean that I could not tell exactly what shade of green their uniform were. However, I could see that they were wearing green-coloured uniforms of the Macedonian Armed Forces." [Interpretation] Did you state this to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Listen, this statement was given by me in 2004, and this is a statement I've given and I'm convinced that they were members of the Macedonian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is how I understood it, that this is what you clarified to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe it would be the time for the recess, for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: All right. We will have our break now and we will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kamberi, if you remember, in your statement to the Prosecutor you stated that when you noticed these individuals wearing military uniforms, you immediately phoned your friend, Avni Iseni, who lived in the Poster neighbourhood. Do you remember stating this?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And your friend, Avni Iseni, came to you immediately. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you know that Avni Iseni is a close relative of Baki Halimi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that he was also involved in the logistics supply to the NLA.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that because of some businesses that your friend Avni Iseni had, he was known as a person who would be able to move through the mountain with his -- with a blindfold and he would still get to Kumanovo. Is that something that was said about your friend, Avni Isni?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you stated in your statement to the Prosecutor, around 4.00 in the morning, you went to the house of Rami Jusufi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you stated that your brother, Meshir was there, Avni Iseni, Rami Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that you stayed there until 5.30 in the morning, in the Rami Jusufi's yard?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you remember what was Rami Jusufi wearing when you were together?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: As far as I know, but still I'm not sure, I think he had jeans on and a T-shirt, a grey T-shirt, dark grey, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask that the witness is now shown Exhibit P1D4. I apologise, exhibit, first P9.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question is whether you recognise in this photograph your friend, Rami Jusufi, and the clothes that he wore that night.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I recognise him. He is a neighbour of mine. He lives 15 metres away from me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you also recognise his clothes as the clothes he wore and what he was wearing at the moment you left his yard?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: These were the same clothes, jeans and a grey T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone would assert before this Court that you were not present on that morning in Rami Jusufi's yard, would you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with that. I was there that morning until 5.30. At that time, I left and went to my children in the lower neighbourhood. So when it started to dawn, I left him at his house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in relation to this question, I wish to indicate the transcript, page 440. If I were to say to you, Mr. Kamberi, that actually you have spent this night not in the yard but in front of the house of Rami Jusufi together with Rami Jusufi, with your brother Meshir, Bajram Jashari, Mesu and Selim Saliu and you were at the check-point in front of that house, that would be the truth. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters wish to ask the counsel to please read the names slowly for the interpreters and for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can read again for the transcript the names of the persons for which I claim were there with you together so I would like to ask whether you agree with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In front of the house of Rami Jusufi there were you, your brother Meshir, Bajram Jashari, Avni Hyseni, Selim Selimi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. We were -- these people, myself, my brother, Rami Jusufi and Avni Hyseni, nobody else was there. Avni lives close to me about 100, 2100, 30 metres away from my house. Rami Jusufi is the next door neighbour. There's only one street, three-metre wide street that divides us, our yards.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to say to you that further down, not far from the church, Memedi Nuri, Memedi Azbi, Memedi Farush, Memedi Qenan and Memedi Nime with his son Sedat were and that they dispatched to you the news that there are some people in the churchyard then, again, these facts would be correct. Can you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That night, until the morning, I was with Avni Jusufi [as interpreted], Meshir and Avni Hyseni. I did not see or speak to anyone else that night. These are the names that you are mentioning. I did not see these people. And in the morning, after 5.30 in the morning, I went to the lower neighbourhood to my uncle Zejnulla Memedi and then I went to sleep.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Tell me, is it correct that the street goes downwards from the church and it goes to the lower part where there is also a meat factory. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask that the witness is shown Prosecutor's Exhibit P148.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have seen this photograph before.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 428.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 428.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please use the marker and show me, draw an arrow to show me how the street goes downwards from the church to the lower part where there is also this meat factory. Actually, just show me the street; it is not necessary to see this meat factory.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: In the photograph, the meat factory is not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Just show me the road that goes downwards from the church to the lower part of the village. Actually, to this cross-road.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, you have marked the churchyard with the number 1 and with the circle. Is that the area of the church?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, the church area.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I then asked you to show me which road goes downwards from the church to the lower part of the village, not from the house of Rami Jusufi but from the church.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: From autobuska [phoen], the road leads to the lower neighbourhood. It goes around the churchyard and then you go straight to the lower neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will like to ask you to draw an arrow up until the place where the decline of the -- the downwards ramp of the street stops and where the street continues going upwards again.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Do you know what? You can see here just 10 percent of the road, to the lower neighbourhood. You don't see the entire road.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I agree. And in this just 10 percent of the road, please show me with an arrow, arrow indicating that this is still going downwards, this part of the street.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes. How can I mark it with an arrow, though, if I cannot see here? Because at Mesanice [phoen] the butcher's shop, on the left, there is a road which goes towards the lower neighbourhood. It's the shortest route, while by car you go around the church and then you go down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you help me like this, Mr. Kamberi, please. Could you draw a circle to mark whether the downward ramp starts of the street from the church towards the area where your houses are and the house of Rami Jusufi that you marked. If you could just draw a circle to indicate where the street stops going downwards, if that can be seen on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That road does not end, because this road goes round the village, the whole village. So there is no end. Goes towards the lower neighbourhood, to the Durmishi neighbourhood and around the village itself. So that's why there is no end to it, because it's a ring road to the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me this now, please, you drew a blue line that has a point or an angle. Is it correct that this part of the road - you say this is a ring road going all throughout the village - that this part of the road, then, goes downwards to the corner that you indicated and then gradually goes upwards to the house of Rami Jusufi and towards your houses and then further through the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: It is correct that this road is the main road that links the whole village but it goes round it. This road leads to the lower neighbourhood, to the Durmishi neighbourhood, to the graveyard, the whole village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Could you now do this: At the corner you made a corner so could you mark it with the number 1?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the place where this line makes a turn.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, there is a turn here. Just around the corner is the entrance to the church.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you to please mark it with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Number 1?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: At the edge?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly here, where you just placed it. And from that point 1, this main road gradually goes uphill towards the house of Rami Jusufi, towards your houses, and other parts of the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: It is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this photograph as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D147, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say to you that at the moment when the armed individuals entered the village in the morning, that fire was opened from this check-point near the church against the police positions at the Straista, then you would agree with me that this is correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I don't agree with what you stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to say to that in that exchange of fire, Rami Jusufi was wounded, then this would also be correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Rami Jusufi was killed by the police and the army, whoever was there and he was killed at the gate of his house, at the door and what you're saying is not true. His -- he was killed at the door of -- to his house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the rest of you withdrew towards the Muslim graveyards. And from that elevation above the Muslim graveyards, you were able to see that at the check-point there are police who are controlling the people leaving the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, checking, instead of controlling.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not understand your question. Could you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A bit later during the day you decided to leave the village. You went by the Muslim graveyards, you went to an elevation from where you were able to see the road going towards Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I was in the village all the time, inside the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And persons who tried to leave the village together with you were Asbi Memedi, Nazim Kamberi, Nuri Memedi, Isali Naim but you did not come to the check-point. You took the fields and reached the river, and this is where you stayed until dusk. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct. That is to say, that somebody who I don't know made a phone call to say that the villagers of Ljuboten should go downhill along the road because buses are coming of the Red Cross or UNHCR, I don't know. But there was this person who said that some buses are coming. And together with all the people from my village, I -- I stayed in the village myself. My children and the whole -- the rest of the village went with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you, Asbi Memedi, Meshir Kamberi, Nuri Memedi, Isali Naim did not go towards the check-point but you were hiding or you were waiting by the river. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Naim Saliu and Asbi Memedi were not people who I met that day. Meshir Kamberi went with the villagers towards the check-point.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when it was known that the villagers were returning to the village, you went to the lower neighbourhood and you stayed there for some time in the house of Asbi Memedi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: No, that is not correct, that I went to Asbi's. I went to my uncle's in the lower neighbourhood. My uncle's name is Selim Memedi.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said that in the evening by accident you heard from Muzafer Jusufi, you learned that Rami Jusufi died. Do you remember stating this in paragraph 19 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I remember that I went -- I met by chance Muzafer Jusufi in the lower neighbourhood, and he told me that Rami was killed and he was at home.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this happened in the evening hours of that day, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: In the evening hours, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If Kenan Salievski, in this statement that I put to you, claimed the following: "[In English] At about 12 hours or 13 hours, Fatmir Kamberi called me and informed me that Rami Jusufi was killed." [Interpretation] Then this would be contrary to what you're saying now, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's not correct. I did not call Qenan Saliu.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ask Muzafer Jusufi when Rami Jusufi died?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I didn't ask him any questions. In the evening, he had set off for Skopje, and I tried to stop him in the lower neighbourhood. I told him to stay there, but he did not agree to what I said. He said, I'll go to Skopje because I can't stay here any longer, and I don't know what happened from then on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Indeed, you met Muzafer Jusufi as he was setting off for Skopje. You didn't see him before that and you didn't know anything about Rami Jusufi's death. This is what you're saying, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Until the evening, before I met Muzafer Jusufi I did not know anything. It was him that told me in the evening that Rami Jusufi had been killed in his house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And at the moment when you saw Muzafer Jusufi he was in fact left for Skopje on that day, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I don't know. He set off in the direction of Skopje. Whether he went there or not, this I don't know, because I didn't see him after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. When you returned in the village with some of your friends, you went to the house of Rami Jusufi and helped his father to take the body of Rami Jusufi at his sister's place in the Durmishi neighbourhood, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the following morning, you yourself attended the funeral of Rami Jusufi in the court yard of his sister, and this ceremony was conducted by the elderly Muslim priest from the village, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Immediately after the funeral of Rami Jusufi, his father Elmaz and mother Zenep left for the place of their other daughter in Skopje and they remained there for over a month, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Elmaz Jusufi has only one daughter, and she's married to somebody in Ljuboten in the Durmishi neighbourhood. He does not have any other daughter. He had two sons and one daughter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. However, I'm asking you whether you're familiar with the fact that Elmaz went to Skopje on that day, together with his wife, and that they remained there for over a month. It looks like the information I had as to where they went in Skopje was not correct.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I don't know myself where they went. They went to Skopje and remained there, but where I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So my question is: They left immediately after the funeral on the 13th of August, and they were not in the village when the OSCE commission that you also mentioned in your statement arrived on the 14th of August in Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if you recall, in your statement you stated that you went to the yard of Rami Jusufi's house and that at that moment certain persons from the OSCE were taking photographs of the bullet casings in the yard. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There was nobody in the house, right, because the father and the mother of Rami Jusufi were already in Skopje, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you saw the body of Rami Jusufi, you would agree with the opinion of Dr. --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, this was a protected witness. So I would kindly ask you to go briefly into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kamberi, is it true that before entering the house of Rami Jusufi, or, rather the house of Elmaz Jusufi, there is a tiled part which is about four to five metres flat?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like now to show the witness Exhibit 1D101.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kamberi, you probably recognise the courtyard and the entry to the house of Elmaz Jusufi, father of Rami Jusufi, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With number 1 - if we could lift up the photograph a little bit, please - is marked the area where the casings were found. Were these casings that you yourself saw when you arrived in Elmaz Jusufi's yard?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: These casings stayed there for several days. That night, in the evening, I did not pass this way, but there is another way to go inside the house, that's how we got Rami. That night we didn't enter this way because you had to go through the churchyard and that was the Macedonian part so we didn't dare go that way. And the bullet casings remained there for two or three days. That night it was dark, and it-- it was not possible for us to see a lot of things.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But later on, when this OSCE commission arrived, you surely saw these casings on this location, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, exactly there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And on this flat part of the yard of Elmaz Jusufi there were these casings, right? And if you can see from the tiles themselves, you would probably say that they are about five metres away from the door that has been damaged by the bullet impact.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to put to you now --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: However, there were other bullet casings at the door, at the gate.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphones of the witness are switched off. The interpreter cannot hear him. Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: The technician is on his way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now the mic is on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I hope you can hear me now, Witness. You earlier said that after the 12th in the evening when you met with Muzafer, you did not see him after this date, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's right, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't see him either on the 14th, when this OSCE commission was there. He was not in the village and you did not see him on this date either, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I don't know, because at that time people did not know where their brothers were. I was staying at my uncle's in the lower neighbourhood while my younger brother went to the city, and my elder brother, I did not know where he was staying, which house. I thought maybe he was staying at a safer house at some other uncle of ours or another cousin, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you did not see him from the moment when you saw him leaving towards Skopje. This is what you explained earlier to me, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I did not see him, and I don't know whether he went to Skopje or not. I know that he set off for Skopje but whether he arrived there, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This was not clear to me; that's why I asked for a clarification. Mr. Kamberi, Dr. Zlatko Jakovski testified before this Trial Chamber, and asked by the Prosecutor: "[In English] Can you please tell us by lower position could this mean that the shooter was in a crouching position or perhaps lying down at the time that the projectile was fired." [Interpretation] The doctor, considering the trajectory of the projectile in the body of Rami Jusufi, stated earlier that the person shooting was at a lower position than Rami Jusufi. This is why the Prosecutor asked the aforementioned question, so that the doctor could clarify his previous statement. So when asked this question the doctor answered the following: "[In English] According to the difference in height of four centimetre between the bone, that is to say, the left inguinal bone and the left side of the body, this is just four centimetres at a very short distance. I can say that the projectile entered the body under the sharp angle of around 50 to 60 degrees with respect to the vertical plane of the body which points to the fact that if the person who is shooting at him, if the person was crouching or lying down, the person would be very close to the deceased. When I say close, I'm just talking about a metre or two, or the deceased might have been at a larger distance from the shooter, but maybe he was on a tree or on the terrace elevated position and the shooter might have been lower." [Interpretation] My question is now, Mr. Kamberi, the following: Is it correct, do you agree with me that Rami Jusufi was not hit at the door to his house, that it happened elsewhere, in front of the entrance to the house on the street or elsewhere. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, Your Honours, I quoted from part of the statement of Dr. Zlatko Jakovski, 2426, and 2427 were the pages quoted. 2427.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that Rami Jusufi was not hit at -- by a bullet at the door of his house?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I am strongly convinced that Rami Jusufi was killed at the entrance door to his house. I don't know who this Zlatko Jakovski is, but they, the doctors, tried even at hospitals to kill the injured and the beaten by the police, those that were beaten in the police stations. Could you please tell me who this world known expert Zlatko Jakovski is?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kamberi, is it correct that the problems related to the village security continued after the events in 2001 and that twice weapons were found once at Basinec locality, five submachine-guns and one automatic weapon. Are you aware of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, five automatic weapons and one semi-automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any knowledge about this.
