utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on the 8th of October, 2001 -- five, 2005, in the village itself, in one part of the village a search was carried out and across the street from the new mosque around 30 hand-held grenades were found, around 1300 bullets, and six automatic rifles. Are you aware of this fact?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it is the police that brings these weapons there to stage everything, this is the strongest evidence that they are the ones who are planting the weapons there and precisely for the purpose of this Tribunal's case. Maybe 2.000, 3.000 children entered that abandoned house in the very centre of the village on daily basis. Nearby there is a shop, excuse my language, but children, adults they entered this house to urinate. This has been planted by the police, and I am a million per cent convinced that this was staged by them at Basinec and at this abandoned house and this was done for the purpose of this trial so that they could gather more evidence, as if to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the course of the search and when weapons were found --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- also the international representatives were present.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Just for the record, I think we're talking about 2005 which is four years after the relevant time period of the indictment so I don't see the relevance of this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters kindly ask the witness to speak in his native language because it is difficult for us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Listen, when it is in my own interest, I would gather not only five different media but 100 when I'm about to stage something that will serve my purpose. They did their calculation, the police, the media, and only to serve their interest here in The Hague. And what you're saying not true and I guarantee you with my own life.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much Mr. Kamberi, you have answered the questions that I have asked you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness, Fatmir Kamberi. My name is Antonio Apostolski, and I am the lead counsel for Mr. Johan Tarculovski and I will ask you questions related to the events in Ljuboten in August 2001. Can I start asking you questions?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that you were born in Ljuboten and that you lived there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You served the conscription military service in Zagreb in 1988 in the infantry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were trained in using infantry weapons during your conscription military service?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: You mean in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, during your conscription military service in Zagreb, in 1988.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct. And that's quite normal for every soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours for the transcript, when I asked my questions in line 8, 1988 is -- 1998 is incorrect. It should have been 1988.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree with me, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you are a member of the political party Democratic Union for Integration, the abbreviation of which is DUI?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction in line 21, 1988.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do support this party, but I'm not a member of it, and I don't have a membership card of this party. But I do support this party, DUI.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown his statement, 2D -- his statement received in evidence today as Exhibit 426, item .5, item 5 on page 3. Could the witness please be shown the respective page in the Albanian language, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the statement in front of you signed -- do you see the paragraph 5?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see that you had stated: "I am a member of the DUI party, Democratic Union for Integration."

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I do support this party. I don't have any document as member of this party, but I do support it, I do help it to the extent that I can. I do represent it, but I don't have a membership card of this party, official membership card. But I do support it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you stated that you were a member of this party? You stated this to the ICTY investigators. You can see this in paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I support it. I will repeat myself again. I support it, I vote for it, and I do help the Democratic Union for Integration, but I don't have an official membership card.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You surely know Ali Ahmeti, he is the president of DUI. Do you know Mr. Ali Ahmeti?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: This is the membership card. It is filled in but it has no seal, nothing of the sort. Look at this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I have asked you --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Ali Ahmeti?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Maybe this was a misunderstanding regarding my membership, so I will answer this. I know Ali Ahmeti -- I apologise. I do know Ali Ahmeti from the media, from rallies.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of transcript, can we record that the witness has shown a DUI membership card which bears no seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is Mr. Ali Ahmeti a member of the Macedonian parliament?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: He is an MP, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was Mr. Ali Ahmeti an MP also in the previous convention of the assembly of the Republic of Macedonia since 2002?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 2001 Ali Ahmeti was the leader of the terrorist organisation NLA?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Listen, you're wrong when you use the term "terrorist." The NLA were not terrorists, neither was Ali Ahmeti. A terrorist wages a secret war, while the NLA waged an open war, fought openly. And the whole world were aware of this war, and all the media as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell me why was the NLA waging war and which were the aims to be achieved?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I can tell you. At this moment you have 100.000 Macedonians without citizenship document, people -- Albanians who were born there, who lived in Macedonia for all their lives, who lived there generation after generation for hundreds of years and they don't have citizenship documents. Secondly, the Macedonian leadership forced the Albanians to take up arms and fight for their rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that they were waging war to attain citizenship status for these 100.000 persons, or did they have other aims as well?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: It's not just a matter of citizenship. Many things have remained unsettled for the Albanians in Macedonia. As far as I know, from 1981 onwards the Albanians in Macedonia didn't have any rights, and I'm speaking precisely about my village. I'm 42 years old. The history does not show that the village of Ljuboten had a single Albanian policeman. Now there are six or seven policemen after the war of 2001, and in all walks of life we were trampled upon and that's why we were forced to take up arms, for our rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the NLA advocating separation of the western part of Macedonia and joining to -- joining it to Albania and Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: This is not true. This is what some of you may think, but this is not what the Albanians wanted then or what they want now. Ali Ahmeti himself demonstrates this clearly. He says this is Macedonia, this is my own fatherland and it is mine as much as it is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you have completed your primary education in your native Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I completed my secondary education in Arsenja Jovkov [phoen] secondary school. Only two subjects were taught in Albanian. The rest were in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that there was a secondary school during that time, Nikola Karev or Zef Ljus Marku in Skopje where the entire teaching was in the Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That is correct. But, tell me, how many classes were there? This was a school, a gymnasium, this Zef Ljus Marku, but the number of classes were previously designated, you could not go over it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that also before 2001 there were Albanian MPs in the Macedonian Assembly?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: It is correct, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that there were members of the government of Albanian ethnicity? I'm now speaking about the time before 2001.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: We still have members in the government, and the European Union and Europe in general, NATO made the Ohrid agreement possible but this Macedonian government is not listening to the Americans, to NATO or to the European Union, let alone to Albanians, those who are members in that Macedonian government.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the second political party in Macedonia after the introduction of a multi-party system that was introduced was the Albanian party, PDP, in 1990?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you can agree with me that immediately after plural party system was introduced, the Albanians were able to establish their party that participated in the first parliamentary elections?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: It is true that they did take part in the elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the first multi-party elections -- I could not give you the exact number but there were around 28 elected MPs, 28 seats in the parliament?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: It is true that there were, but what choice did they have? Nothing.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the previous question should have been "is it true that they won 28 seats in the parliament. The Question now is --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true there were members in the government of the Republic of Macedonia of Albanian ethnicity after the first parliamentary elections?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me now, who is the president of the branch of DUI in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Sadri Halimi.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that there are many supporters of DUI in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's true. And the party of Ali Ahmeti always comes victorious in the elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Ejup Amitov is a distinguished member of DUI from the Ljuboten village, or Ejup Ahmeti?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: To my knowledge, he is not a member of the BDI, or DUI. I don't know if things have changed recently, but to my knowledge, he is not a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the NLA members became DUI members?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know Xhezair Shaqiri, he was a MP in the assembly of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Xhezair Shaqiri is not a member of parliament. He is not a MP now. I know him because of the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that he was a MP in the previous convention? I asked you about that assembly, the one of 2002.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: He was then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that Xhezair Shaqiri is known as Commander Hodza?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And he was a NLA commander. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Xhezair Shaqiri proclaimed in August 2007, that the part of Macedonia where Tanusevci village is located will take cessation from Macedonia and will be joined to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: The politicians know these things better. I'm not aware of this. Xhezair must know and the Macedonian government and the rest of the politicians. I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did the Commander Hodza -- did Xhezair Shaqiri proclaim this through the media, through the Macedonian media? This was at the end of August. This was some 15 days ago.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I know this, that he publicly denied that those were his words. He publicly said that those were words were attributed to him wrongly. He never said them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. On Friday, August 10, 2001, you were at your home with your family. Is that correct? I'm speaking about the morning, yes.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You woke up around 8.00. The shelling of the village of Ljubanci woke you up -- I apologise. You woke up around 8.00 from the noise of the shelling of the village?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The shelling lasted until 11.00, and it came from the positions of the Macedonian security forces direction. They were located at Malistena or Tumba.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that more than 30 shells impacted during that time?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Listen, I can't give you an exact number. Maybe there were 40, maybe 20, or 25. I can't tell you how many shells there were. I know only of some shells that fell on houses, on the roofs of the houses, but as to how many there were, I cannot know.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the shells caused damage? Several houses were set on fire by that?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: The barn of Haxhi Dalipi was burned because of the shelling. I'm speaking about the flames that we -- that were seen, because there were other houses that were damaged by shelling, and Haxhi Dalipi's barn was burned. We could see the flames.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown N005-7605. Could the photograph please be zoomed in. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell us approximately where is the barn that you mentioned where the shell fell, so that this part of the photograph could be zoomed in. In which corner of the photograph? Could you show this?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: If you zoom in on the right, on my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the photograph please be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Towards the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in the right corner of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you now see it in this photograph? And mark it with a circle.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Of course. I placed a dot here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark it with number 1?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark in this photograph other houses where shells fell on the morning of August 10, 2001, the houses that were damaged?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: The houses that were damaged. Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark them with numbers 2 or 3 or 4. If there are several of them?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Which day are you referring to? Could you please explain to me which date.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Friday, 10th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: The barn -- the barn of Haxhi Murati [phoen] was not burned on Friday. That Dalip Murati's barn or stable was burned on the 12th of August. Whether it was a Zolja or a RPG, I don't know. I was at my uncle's house Zejnulla Memedi's house which is 50 metres away from there. That I saw with my own eyes because I was hiding there behind the wall. On Friday --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Since you stated that several shells fell on the Friday --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I will tell you now about Friday. Nuredin Elezi's house was hit on the roof. Because it is in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark it with the number 2. Approximately, not necessarily the exact house. The part where it is.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I can give the exact place of the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please mark the house with number 2.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark another house, if you're aware of another house having been hit on Friday morning.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: It was the house of Veli Esati, but it is not here in the photograph. It's on my left, here on the photograph. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Could you see in this photograph another house that was hit on Friday morning, on the 10th of August?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Nuredin Elezi's house was hit. Veli Esati's house, Ismail's house, I can't remember his surname now, or maybe Ismaili was his surname. Several shells fell --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please just mark them?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Let me just tell you, this photograph -- but you have to move the photograph a little bit to the right, because those houses cannot be seen here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this photograph be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D48, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think this would be a convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Okay. We will have our break until 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Kamberi, you stated that you were employed at the post office. You were working there. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you left the service since you were involved in financial embezzlements at the post office?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you worked together with Blagoja Stojanovksi there at the post office?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Do you drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Never in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you would go to the bars in the Cair municipality after work with your colleagues from the post office?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: It is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you went together with Blagoja in the -- to a bar in the vicinity of the sports centre Karpos and that you drank alcohol there?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, Partizan and not Karpos.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. I did not drink alcohol though. My friends did.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you discussed the events of August 2001 in Ljuboten with Blagoja there at the bar?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the addendum to his statement received today as Exhibit P426. So 2D00-355. If we could go to page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If you could look at item 2 at that says: "During the conversation with Blagoja Stojanovski that took place about five or six months ago in the cafe in the vicinity of Partizan recreation centre in Cair, he talked about the incident in Ljubanci village which killed Macedonian soldiers. At the beginning of conversation we were all consuming alcohol and later on, the quantity increased which provoked Blagoja to speak even more." Is it correct that you have stated this to the OTP of this Tribunal, that you drank alcohol with him together?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This means that you consume alcohol, although you told us earlier that you don't.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: No. What I said was that I never even tried alcohol in my whole life. I was present there. I consumed coffee, alcohol -- correction, Coca-Cola but not alcohol. My friends did consume alcohol. Personally, I didn't try alcohol in all my live.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You told the investigators that there is a family relation between Blagoja and Johan Tarculovski. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct. According to his words.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you told them that Blagoja told you that in the school-yard in Ljubanci, Johan Tarculovski climbed on the top of the staircase of the school and held a speech. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct. According to his words.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This means that the information you received was from Blagoja Stojanovski, your colleague, right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the statement of Blagoja Stojanovski, 2D356. He provided this statement to the Defence of Johan Tarculovski on the 3rd of September, 2005. This statement has a draft translation, which was done by Defence members of Johan Tarculovski. If we could go to this statement, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In his statement given on the 3rd of September 2007 [as interpreted] Mr. Blagoja Stojanovski said the following: "I never had the last name Cajkulov [phoen], my surname was Stojanovski. I work at the post office as a main cashier. When asked about Fatmir Kamberi, I know his name because of the following: Before the year 2005, a person with that name worked at the post office in Cair. I know this name because he was caught in the crime of theft in the post office and that's why he was dismissed from work. I know this person very little. We worked at the same post office, maybe we sat together in the -- in the post office itself but never outside in a cafe." I was in my house in Ljubanci in August 2001, when eight members of the Macedonian army were killed. Amongst them was Tomca Badarovski [phoen], a colleague. All of the other colleagues from the post office went to the funeral. Everyone was aware of that, all of my colleagues from the post office knew I was there at the funeral; I'm not hiding that. There was a large group of people who were paying tribute to the killed people from the village. I remember that people from the army were making a speech and they -- there were honour fires in tribute of the killed. I don't remember anyone giving a speech. I don't remember anyone else giving a speech." Asked about the person Johan Tarculovski, I know him since his parents come from his village and now I know him better after he was arrested by the ICTY. Asked whether this person was at Ljubanci village August 10 to 12, 2001. I state that I haven't seen him then. Even if he had been there, I couldn't have seen him because there was a huge crowd of people."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you agree with me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I note that several moments several minutes ago at the top of this page the witness was mentioned. However, the Prosecution believes it is not an appropriate use -- it is not an appropriate form of cross-examination than to simply to continue to read into the record information about events that very well may have nothing to do with this witness. There's a question about what is said about the witness in -- on this statement. That question should have been put to the witness several minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I'm sure, Mr. Apostolski, that you will be able to adapt your questioning to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will adhere to the previous examination, because in my previous questions also these topics were comprised. The topics comprised by the addendum to the statement of the witness that is received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that you worked at the post office. You remember that? And -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: It is correct that I used to work there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were dismissed from work at the post office? You were dismissed because of embezzlement?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: That is not correct. That's not correct. I had an argument with Tahir Jakupi, the general director in his office because they did not give me a decision. I have witnesses and there are witnesses who can testify to my going to his office and having the argument with him, because he did not issue the decision that he had promised.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Blagoja Stojanovski, when asked about you, stated that: "The person, Fatmir Kamberi, is known to me because sometime before 2005, a person by that name worked at the post office in Cair. He came to my knowledge because he was caught in the act of theft at the post office. He embezzled a large amount of money and this is why he was dismissed. I know this person very little. We used to work at the same post office. Maybe we would sit together at the post office." Do you agree with the statement of Mr. Blagoja Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you sat with Blagoja Stojanovski at the In Direkta [phoen] cafe near the sports centre Partizan in Cair and he spoke to you about the events at Ljubanci village?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct. And every day after working hours we went to that cafe, all of us, workers of the post office.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Blagoja Stojanovski stated: "We never sat together outside of the post office at any cafe or a bar when the Defence asked about the person Fatmir Kamberi." So could you agree with me that Mr. Blagoja Stojanovski states that he never went to a cafe or a bar with you?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I will tell you, and you can be convinced that every day after working hours, he was there. He is a drunkard; he drinks a lot of alcohol. And you can ask anybody working at the post office, whether Blagoja Stojanovski drinks or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But Mr. Blagoja Stojanovski states that he never sat with you together. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. It is not. I swear it is not correct. We stayed together 200 times at the least.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you had indicated in your statement that Mr. Johan Tarculovski made a speech in the school-yard in Ljubanci and that Mr. Blagoja Stojanovski had seen that speech and then he communicated that to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Listen, all the words I have stated in my statements -- in my statement I'm not denying here. According to what Blagoja Stojanovski said, I was not there in the Ljubance. I did not see anything with my own eyes, but because of the alcohol and he was also involved in arguments with people and fights because of the alcohol, and he said things about Ljuboten, the war in Ljuboten and Ljubance. How could I say these sentences? I'm repeating again. This is according to his words because I was not present there, I did not see anything myself. He was completely drunk.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But Mr. -- however, Mr. Blagoja Stojanovski states that Johan Tarculovski is known to him because his parents come from his village, and "I know him now as person arrested by the ICTY." And, further, on he states: "I haven't seen this person at the village of Ljubanci at August 10 to 12, 2001. Even if he had been there, I did not see him. There was a huge crowd of people." Is this in contradiction with what you stated to the ICTY investigators, in relation to what Blagoja Stojanovski stated to you in relation to -- or about the Ljuboten events at August 10 to 12, 2001? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. According to his words. Again, I will repeat: I did not see it myself, I was not present there to see who spoke, who held a speech and who participated. But according to Blagoja Stojanovski's words, that's what happened. I don't know anything further. Whatever he told me, I related. I didn't add anything, I did not take away anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that there is a family relation between him and Johan Tarculovski; that is, between Blagoja Stojanovski and Johan Tarculovski. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Correct. Every time when he spoke he said, He's my bratucet, my uncle's son. I don't know whether this is true or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: However, Mr. Blagoja Stojanovski in his statement says the following, that Johan Tarculovski is known to him because his parents come from his village and now I know him as one of the detainees The Hague Tribunal. Would you agree with me that Mr. Blagoja Stojanovski states that he has no kinship relation with Johan Tarculovski and this is completely in contradiction with what you have stated?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Well, I cannot force him to be his uncle's son. His mouth uttered these words. So how can I say that of my own will? How can I say Tahir Hasani, an ex-person, is my uncle's son if he is not? I did not create this. I don't really know whether he was a cousin or whether he was boasting about it. Maybe they were or they are cousins. What I'm relating here are his words and his words were that, He is my bratucet, my cousin.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we have displayed Exhibit P5. It's the same photo that my learned colleague showed but without the markings.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Kamberi, you were asked about the bullet casings that we can see in the photo. You started explaining there were also more bullet casings elsewhere when you went to the house of Rami Jusufi afterwards. Where did you see these other bullet casings?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I saw the other casings at the iron gate, the one that takes you from the street into the yard, and every house in that neighbourhood by the road, the shop included, the shop near the bus-stop, they had locks and these locks were destroyed by firing from a short distance with Kalashnikovs. The entire street was full of casings. I'm not speaking about Rami Jusufi's gate only, the entire road had casings.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Interrupt you and let's focus now on Rami Jusufi's case. Did you see also bullets somewhere else, in addition to near the gate?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: At the iron gate, the one that you can see here before the entrance to the house and a little bit more in the rear, there is a fountain, water fountain there, and there there were also some casings.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Maybe if we could have the usher's assistance with the pens or... You could please draw a circle where you saw the bullets and then write different numbers in the different locations.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: I cannot see that place here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please draw an arrow indicating the direction where was the gate.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: 1, it is in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please draw an arrow indicating the direction.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And could you please write number 2.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: You cannot see the place itself here on the photograph, but two metres from the place where the casings are, more in the rear, there is a water fountain, and there is a concrete fence, and there there were casings too.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please write number 2 next to the arrow so we know that you are referring to the water container?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you see bullet casings somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you see any bullet impact?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes. There were bullet impacts. As I said, the padlock of the main gate was destroyed by bullet impact. And also, at the entry to the house, to the hall of the house, there was a bullet impact on the window-frame, and the door itself is made of wood and there are some traces of bullets there as well. And opposite to the hall, they had their kitchen and some bullets hit that kitchen too.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Kamberi, when you refer to the door, are you referring to the wooden door that we can see at the end of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: Yes. I saw the holes there and also on the gate by the main road. The padlock had these traces of bullet impact, as they were trying to unlock the gate by using Kalashnikovs.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Obviously we cannot see the gate here, but if you could please draw a circle in the wooden door where you saw the impacts and write number 3 next to it.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR KAMBERI
utterances.text: However, you cannot see the bullet-holes here, only the window on the right-hand side, while the holes near the padlock cannot be seen clearly on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please write number 3. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I would like to tender into evidence this photo, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P429, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: No more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You will be -- is there any scope for re-examination, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: So you will be very pleased, Mr. Kamberi, that this brings an end to your examination. You are free to go home now and to return to your activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. Do I have the right to pose a question to the Defence, a brief question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: No, that's not possible in the proceedings here. You may discuss this after the hearing, but not at this moment in time. So the usher will now show you out and we thank you for your contribution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Allow me to say something to all those present in this courtroom. They say that in the village of Ljuboten, and they insist, in fact, that there was NLA in the village, I would just say one thing for all of you. There was no NLA in Ljuboten village. The NLA --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kamberi, that is the end of your evidence. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- wherever the NLA entered, free zones were proclaimed afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, I see we have seven minutes left. Is this still a useful moment to call your new witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Our next witness is arriving in The Hague probably right about this moment, so he will be ready to testify tomorrow morning, Dr. Stein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: So we will then adjourn for the day and resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
